prompt.context: Our client, Red & Blue Airlines Group, is based in Santiago, Chile and has operations to many cities across the globe. Its most iconic route is Santiago – Puerto Natales. The managing director of Network Planning needs your help: he wants to increase quality in this market.
prompt.question: How would you approach increasing the quality (customer experience) on the Santiago – Puerto Natales route? What are the main drivers behind the recent decrease in customers, and how would you prioritize solutions?

clarifying_info.q: What are the revenue sources for this route?
How long has the company operated this route, and is there competition?
clarifying_info.a: The company has operated this market for 10 years and has no competition.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the typical customers on this route?
clarifying_info.a: The market has a premium leisure component; those passengers are also corporate passengers during the rest of the year.

clarifying_info.q: What has been the recent trend in passengers and cargo?
clarifying_info.a: During the last two years, there has been an increase in Cargo but a decrease in customers. There are some internal causes but also external ones. The goal is to increase customer experience.

exhibits.title: Net Promoter Score – Customer Satisfaction Analysis
exhibits.shows: A chart comparing Net Promoter Score (NPS) driver scores between 2018 and 2020 across multiple service dimensions.

data.note: Scores are shown for 2018 and 2020. Cabin crew = friendliness, attention, efficiency, and attitude. IFE = In-flight entertainment.

exhibits.title: Punctuality Analysis – Delay Causes and On-Time Performance by Time Block
exhibits.shows: Two charts: (left) a scatter plot of delay causes plotted by hours of delay (x-axis) vs. number of customers affected (y-axis), with causes labeled as internal or external; (right) a table of % of flights on time by time block (AM Prime, AM, Noon, PM, PM Prime, Night).

left_chart.note: Passengers affected 3 hours or more need to be compensated, generating additional costs.

exhibits.title: Punctuality Analysis – Market Data for Quantitative Calculation
exhibits.shows: A table with four data items: total market customers, the client's market weight, customer schedule split, and punctuality improvement targets.

data.Customer schedule: AM: 50% of company PAX, AM Prime: 70% of company PAX (% who travel in each time block — note: figures represent on-time share in those blocks, cross-reference with Part 1)
data.note: AM and AM Prime improvement figures represent the potential uplift in on-time performance achievable.

framework: Customer journey lens across four phases: Interest/Awareness (price, booking experience), Pre-Trip (information, customer service), On-Trip (safety, punctuality, in-flight experience), Post-Trip (customer service, retention).
Identify root causes of the decrease in customers — distinguish internal (controllable) vs. external (non-controllable) drivers.
Prioritize pain points using an Impact–Complexity matrix: focus first on high-impact, low-complexity (quick wins) internal improvements.
For the top priority (punctuality): quantify the affected passenger base and the revenue/cost impact of improvement, then propose operational solutions.
Assess financial implications of proposed solutions (CAPEX vs. OPEX) and operational ripple effects before recommending.

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 1 (NPS evolution 2018–2020), what are the main drivers of the decrease in customers?
questions.guidance: A strong answer identifies the three dimensions with the largest NPS decline: Punctuality (dropped from ~20 to 3), Seat Comfort (dropped from 10 to 2 or similar), and Brand Perception (dropped from 7 to 3). Candidate should note these are the priority areas. Punctuality stands out as both high-magnitude and potentially actionable internally.

questions.prompt: Where should the client focus attention and how would you prioritize? Brainstorm solutions and discuss implications.
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose using an Impact–Complexity matrix. Punctuality should be prioritized as high impact and lower complexity (internal fixes available). Seat comfort requires capital investment (higher complexity/CAPEX). Brand perception is harder to address directly and may follow from punctuality improvements. Implications span: Financial (CAPEX for seat refurbishment, OPEX for operational changes), Operations (schedule changes, maintenance scheduling), and Marketing (communications around improvements). Interviewer should push candidate toward focusing on the punctuality issue.

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 2 Part 1, analyze the delay causes. Which should the client focus on first?
questions.guidance: Candidate should mentally build a 2x2 matrix (high/low delay hours vs. high/low passengers affected). Internal causes (Unscheduled Maintenance, Crew Expiration, Operational Planning, Workshop Management, Fleet Availability) are quick wins — controllable by the client. External causes (Weather, Airport Capacity) are harder to address. The highest-impact internal cause visible in the scatter is Unscheduled Maintenance (high on both axes). Candidate should note that passengers delayed 3+ hours trigger compensation costs, adding financial urgency.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2 Part 2, calculate how many additional passengers the client could recover if punctuality improvements are achieved.
questions.guidance: Walk through the four-step calculation. A great candidate sets up market sizing first, then applies the improvement percentage, and interprets the ~18% improvement as meaningful context for a recommendation.

math.setup: Step 1: Find client's current PAX base. Step 2: Split by time block (AM vs AM Prime). Step 3: Find current on-time PAX per block. Step 4: Apply punctuality improvement % to find additional on-time PAX. Step 5: Compute overall % improvement.
steps: Market customers = 24M × 10% market weight = 2.4M company PAX
(Note: 30%/70% split implied; AM block currently 50% on time, AM Prime 70% on time)
PAX currently on time — AM: 50% × 720K = 360K  |  AM Prime: 70% × 1,680K = 1,176K

Improvement — AM: +5% uplift × 720K ≈ 36K additional  |  AM Prime: +14% uplift × 1,176K ≈ 235K additional  (improvement %s derived from target uplifts: AM 10% improvement on 50% base = +5pp; AM Prime 20% improvement on 70% base = +14pp)
math.answer: Approximately 271,000 additional passengers served on time, representing ~18% improvement in on-time PAX across AM and AM Prime time blocks.

brainstorming.prompt: Where should the client focus attention and how would you prioritize solutions? What are the implications of each?

categories.name: Punctuality – Internal fixes (Quick Wins)
ideas: Improve maintenance scheduling to reduce unscheduled maintenance events
Optimize crew scheduling to avoid crew expiration delays
Improve operational planning and boarding processes
Better workshop management and fleet availability tracking

categories.name: Punctuality – External mitigation
ideas: Negotiate with airports for priority slots in high-disruption periods
Build buffer time into schedules for weather-prone time blocks
Develop contingency protocols for airport disruptions

categories.name: Seat Comfort
ideas: Invest in seat refurbishment or aircraft reconfiguration (CAPEX)
Prioritize higher-margin leisure/premium routes for upgraded seating
Communicate improvement timeline to manage customer expectations

categories.name: Brand Perception
ideas: Brand perception likely improves downstream as punctuality and comfort improve
Targeted loyalty programme or communications campaign for the Santiago–Puerto Natales route
Leverage corporate passenger segment as ambassadors

categories.name: Prioritization framework
ideas: Use Impact–Complexity matrix: high impact + low complexity = do first (punctuality internal fixes)
High impact + high complexity = plan with investment (seat comfort)
Low impact items (IFE, booking process) deprioritize for now

recommendation: The three main drivers of the customer decrease are Punctuality, Seat Comfort, and Brand Perception, as evidenced by the NPS decline from 2018 to 2020.

The client should prioritize internal punctuality improvements (unscheduled maintenance, crew scheduling, operational planning) as these are controllable and can recover approximately 271,000 on-time passengers (~18% improvement) on the AM and AM Prime blocks.
Seat comfort improvements require CAPEX investment and should be planned for a subsequent phase once the operational quick wins are implemented.
risks: Any schedule change could impact the rest of the network operation — interdependencies must be assessed before implementing time-block changes.
Punctuality and seat improvement investments depend on the company's financial situation; CAPEX availability must be confirmed.
External factors such as weather and airport capacity remain difficult to control and may limit total punctuality improvement.
next_steps: Understand the full trade-off of proposed solutions (cost vs. passenger recovery impact).
Shift or adjust flights currently in low on-time time blocks (AM Prime at 50%, Night at 50%) to configurations that can achieve 100% on-time performance.
Quantify the investment required to improve seat comfort and build the business case.
Monitor NPS on an ongoing basis after punctuality improvements to track impact on brand perception.
